name: Chip supply
summary: Helium shortage and the 10 Nov rare-earth deadline weigh on chip supply
state: Qatar supplies about a third of the world's helium, which chip fabs need, and Hormuz disruption has tightened supply, though Oxford Economics says the sector has enough for now (Gowling WLG; Oxford Economics). China's rare-earth control pause expires on 10 Nov. Chip shares fell sharply on 5 Nov, but no TSMC or Samsung output stoppage has been reported.
for_you: Electronics buyers may see longer lead times on some components.
rubric_hit: Shortage risk in key inputs = Watch; no major fab disruption

sources.title: Gowling WLG — Helium, Hormuz and the chip supply chain
Oxford Economics — Chip sector has enough helium, for now

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
